F reaches B, C and D in one hop and A in three, so it scores 0.67, ahead of E 0.50 and G 0.33." width="100%"} Closeness measures how few steps a node needs to reach the nodes on the *other* side of a bipartite graph. For each node in the chosen partition, the method finds hop-count distances (edge weights are ignored) to every node in the opposite partition and returns the reciprocal of the average distance. A node adjacent to every node on the other side scores `1.0`; nodes that need longer paths score lower. The partitions are those returned by `bipartite_sets()`. Restricting the average to the opposite partition makes the scores reflect how directly a node is tied to the "other kind" of entity, which suits questions like: - which members can reach all events through the fewest intermediaries? - which papers are closest to the whole community of authors? - which diseases are most directly connected to the full set of genes? Only nodes in the chosen partition are scored. Unreachable nodes in the opposite partition are left out of the average, so in a disconnected graph a node is scored only against the part of the other side it can reach, and a node that can reach none of it scores `0.0`. If the opposite partition is empty, every score is `0.0`. The method runs a graph traversal from every node in the chosen partition, so its cost grows roughly with the size of that partition times the size of the graph. On directed graphs edge direction is ignored, so distances are those of the underlying undirected graph. The whole graph is used and the current selection is ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [which]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Which partition to compute centrality for: `0` (default) or `1`. Partitions are numbered as in `bipartite_sets()`: in each connected component, partition `0` is the side that contains the component's lowest node ID. Any other value raises an error. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node DataFrame column the scores are written to. If `None` (default), the column is named `"bipartite_closeness_centrality"`. Only nodes in the chosen partition are written: if the column is new, the other nodes get null values; if it already exists, their existing values are kept. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `False` (default), returns the graph itself so calls can be chained, and records the computation so it is listed by `describe()`. If `True`, returns the scores as a dictionary instead, without writing anything to the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping each node ID in the chosen partition to its closeness score (range `[0, 1]`). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): the graph itself, for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not bipartite, or if `which=` is not `0` or `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this people-film network the films are partition `1`. "Film2" is one hop from three people and three hops from "Ann", for an average distance of `1.5` and a score of `1 / 1.5 = 0.667`; "Film3", on the edge of the network, scores lowest: ::: {#77fce953 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["Ann", "Bob", "Cal", "Dee", "Film1", "Film2", "Film3"]) .add_edges( [ ("Ann", "Film1"), ("Bob", "Film1"), ("Bob", "Film2"), ("Cal", "Film2"), ("Cal", "Film3"), ("Dee", "Film2"), ] ) ) scores = graph.bipartite_closeness_centrality(which=1, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(score, 3) for nid, score in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'Film1': 0.5, 'Film2': 0.667, 'Film3': 0.333} ``` ::: ::: With the default `return_dict=False` the scores are stored in the node DataFrame instead. Scoring the people (partition `0`) under a custom column name shows "Bob" and "Cal", who sit in the middle of the network, ahead of "Ann" and "Dee"; the films have no value in this column: ::: {#03673be0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( graph .bipartite_closeness_centrality(which=0, attr_name="closeness_to_films") .get_node_df() .select(["label", "closeness_to_films"]) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
